reports.title: Vancouver, BC, November 5th, 2026 - NexGen Energy Ltd. (TSX: NXE) (NYSE: NXE) (ASX: NXG) ("NexGen" or the "Company") will host its 2026 third quarter conference call on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, at 8:00 am Eastern Time.

desk.headline: Pre-revenue uranium developer; net loss narrows to C$22.3m on debenture revaluation gain; Rook I construction under way, no financial guidance

other.label: Spending on Rook I plant and equipment (Q3)

results: NexGen has no revenue yet; the Q3 net loss shrank to C$22.3m (C$0.03 a share) from C$129.2m, mainly because its convertible debentures were revalued at a C$25.6m gain versus a C$95.2m loss a year ago.
Operating costs rose to C$47.7m, driven by share-based pay of C$30.1m and higher admin and travel costs as the project team grows.
Construction spending at the Rook I uranium project picked up, with about C$105m spent on plant and equipment in the quarter.
Cash and short-term investments totalled C$821.6m, plus 2.7m pounds of uranium held as strategic inventory (C$341.2m at cost).
Holders converted the remaining US$110m of 2023 debentures into shares (US$40m in September, US$70m in October), cutting debt.

guidance.summary: NexGen gives no revenue or earnings guidance. Its outlook covers Rook I project steps, with shaft freezing and pre-sinking planned to start in Q1 2027; it says more funding will be needed to finish construction.

points: Licensed construction began on 8 June 2026, and the shaft-sinking contract was awarded in September.
Q4 work focuses on shaft preparations, detailed engineering, signing more major contracts and finishing the airstrip.
The latest pre-production cost estimate is still about C$2.2bn from the 2024 interim update; extra financing will be needed.
Drilling on the Patterson Corridor East target was about two-thirds done at end-September, with completion expected in early December.
call.source: Management's discussion and analysis (Exhibit 99.2); no call coverage found

watch: How and when NexGen raises the remaining funding for Rook I construction.
Start of shaft pre-sinking in Q1 2027 and any update to the capital cost estimate.
Swings in reported results from debenture revaluations and the uranium price.
